who.text: The TSP (the utility that owns the wires) decides, builds, owns and recovers the cost from load through its transmission cost of service. A wholesale battery does not pay it ([[16 TAC 25.192]]).
who.label: REAL

who.lead: A new line needs a permit; a reconductor does not.
who.text: A new line needs a PUCT certificate (a CCN). Rebuilding on the existing right of way or reconductoring does not ([[16 TAC 25.101]]). A ratings change is a neutral [[Tier 4]] project that ERCOT does not review.
who.label: REAL

who.text: [[Tier 1]] projects of {TIER1_MUSD} or more need the ERCOT Board; a [[Tier 2]] project under that with a CCN gets a review of {TIER2_DAYS}. Everything else is [[Tier 3 or 4]].
who.label: REAL

who.lead: A battery owner can ask, and can pay for its own connection.
who.text: It can propose a project to the Regional Planning Group ([[NP 3.11.4.1]]), offer to fund one the TSP chooses to pursue, and pay interconnection facilities above {ALLOWANCE_138_MUSD} (at [[138 kV]] and below) or {ALLOWANCE_ABOVE_MUSD} (above). It cannot order, own, schedule or fund a network upgrade on its own.
who.label: REAL

who.lead: Storage is not a transmission alternative in ERCOT today.
who.text: Planning treats it as a dispatchable resource. [[SB 415]] lets a utility contract for storage, but only for distribution reliability, up to {SB415_CAP_MW}, and the utility may not own it.
who.label: REAL
